passage:
Counsellor's note, 9 October. Kashish.
Vishal, Class 10, came to my room after lunch and sat without speaking for a while.
In summer he met someone in a gaming chat who said they were sixteen. The chats moved to a private app, then to questions about his family, then to a request for a photo "just for fun", and last week to a plan to meet at the mall, alone.
He said he felt flattered at first, then stuck, because the person knew so much about him. He kept apologising. I told him clearly that none of this is his fault and that coming to me was exactly right.
Next steps, today: called his mother, who came in by three. Together we saved the chats, blocked and reported the account, and contacted the cybercrime helpline. No meeting will happen. I will check in with Vishal on Monday.

qa.q: Where did Vishal first meet the person?
qa.a: Vishal met the person in a gaming chat in summer.

qa.q: Why did Vishal feel stuck?
qa.a: He felt flattered at first, then trapped, because the person already knew so much about him.

qa.q: Which steps did Kashish take the same day?
qa.a: Kashish told Vishal it was not his fault, called his mother, and with them saved the chats, blocked and reported the account, and contacted the cybercrime helpline.

qa.q: How might Vishal's mother feel when she arrives at three?
qa.a: She may be frightened and upset, but relieved that Vishal spoke up and that the school acted quickly.

grounding: A counsellor records how a boy's online contact moved him to a private app, personal questions, a photo request and a meeting plan, and how they acted that day.

passage:
14 Nov, night
Sky from the art group has messaged me for a month. Sky says I'm mature for fifteen, that my drawings are better than any adult's. At first it felt amazing, like finally someone sees me.
Then it was: let's talk on a different app. Then: what are you wearing in your room right now? Tonight Sky asked me to take the bus to the city on Saturday, just us, and not tell anyone.
I felt sick and flattered at the same time, which makes no sense.
I called Amandeep Masi, because she never makes me feel stupid. She came over in twenty minutes, said I was brave and it wasn't my fault. We showed Mummy together. Mummy held my hand while Masi helped us report and block the account. Tomorrow we're telling Ma'am at school.
I'm not going Saturday. I'm sleeping in Mummy's room tonight.
Chandrika

qa.q: Where did Sky ask Chandrika to go on Saturday?
qa.a: Sky asked Chandrika to take the bus to the city on Saturday.

qa.q: What did Chandrika feel about Sky's attention?
qa.a: Chandrika felt sick and flattered at the same time, enjoying being seen but alarmed by the secret trip.

qa.q: Why was calling Amandeep Masi the right step?
qa.a: Masi came quickly, said it wasn't Chandrika's fault, and helped tell Mummy and report and block the account that night, so no meeting happens.

qa.q: How might Mummy feel holding Chandrika's hand?
qa.a: Mummy likely feels scared and upset about Sky, but relieved that Chandrika told a trusted adult in time.

grounding: A teen flattered by an online contact is pushed to a private app, personal questions and a secret meeting, then tells an aunt who acts with the parent that night.

passage:
For three weeks, Aparna had been chatting with "Rahul, 17" from a gaming app. He was funny. He said she was mature for fourteen. Then he asked her to move to a private messaging app. Then he asked what she wore to school, where her building was, and on Friday night, for a photo.
Aparna felt flattered and stuck at the same time. If she said no, he might get angry. If she said yes, something felt wrong.
She knocked on her brother Chetan's door. He was nineteen. "Bhaiya, can I show you something? Don't be mad."
Chetan read the chat and took a deep breath. "I'm not mad at you. You did nothing wrong. This isn't okay, though. Let's tell Mumma now."
Mumma was in the kitchen. She dried her hands, read the chat, and hugged Aparna. "Thank you for telling us." That night they took screenshots, blocked him, and reported the account to the cyber-crime helpline together.

qa.q: What did Rahul ask for on Friday night?
qa.a: For a photo.

qa.q: How did Aparna feel when Rahul asked for more?
qa.a: Aparna felt flattered and stuck, worried he'd get angry if she said no, but sensing something was wrong.

qa.q: What steps kept Aparna safe?
qa.a: She told Chetan, they told Mumma straight away, and that night they took screenshots, blocked him and reported the account to the cyber-crime helpline.

qa.q: How did Mumma react when she read the chat?
qa.a: Mumma stayed calm and loving, hugging Aparna and thanking her for telling them.

grounding: It shows a teen flattered and stuck as an online contact moves to private apps, personal questions and a photo request, and telling trusted adults that night.

passage:
"Tanuja Masi, can I tell you something? You won't tell me off?"
"Gopika, I promise I won't. What is it?"
"There's this boy I met in an online game. He says he's sixteen. We talk every day. He moved us to another app so it's 'just us.'"
"Okay. I'm listening."
"Now he keeps asking where I live and what school I go to. Yesterday he asked for a picture. In my night clothes."
Tanuja kept her voice steady. "Thank you for telling me. You are not to blame for any of this. Did you send anything?"
"No. But I felt bad saying no. He's been so nice."
"Feeling flattered is normal. He's the one doing something wrong, not you. Can you show me the chat?"
Gopika handed over the phone.
"We'll screenshot it, block him, and tell your Mumma together, right now. Then we'll report it on the cyber-crime portal tonight."
Gopika nodded, and her shoulders dropped.

qa.q: What did the boy ask for yesterday?
qa.a: A picture. In night clothes.

qa.q: How did Gopika feel about saying no to him?
qa.a: Gopika felt bad and guilty about saying no, because he'd been so nice, even though something felt wrong.

qa.q: What did Tanuja Masi do that a trusted adult should?
qa.a: She stayed calm, told Gopika there was no blame on Gopika, and planned to screenshot, block, tell Gopika's Mumma right away and report it that night.

qa.q: How might Tanuja have felt hearing about the night-clothes request?
qa.a: Tanuja probably felt alarmed and protective, but kept her voice steady so Gopika would feel safe.

grounding: It shows a teen flattered and stuck as an online contact asks personal questions and for a picture, and a trusted aunt responding calmly the same night.

passage:
I'm Ganga, and when I was fifteen, I thought Tejas was my best friend. We met in a comments section under a music video. He said he was seventeen, from Pune. He was sweet. He remembered everything I told him.
After a month he said, "Let's talk on a private app, just us." Then he asked what time my parents got home. Then for photos. Then he said he'd come to my city to meet me, at the mall, alone. "Don't tell anyone. They'll ruin it."
I felt flattered and trapped at once. I didn't want to lose him. I also didn't want to go.
The next morning I told my class teacher before assembly. She listened without any shock in her face and said, "You're not to blame. You did exactly the right thing." She called my mother right then, and together they reported the account to the police cyber cell that afternoon.
I never went to the mall.

qa.q: Where did Tejas want to meet Ganga?
qa.a: At the mall, alone.

qa.q: How did Ganga feel when Tejas asked to meet?
qa.a: Ganga felt flattered and trapped at once, not wanting to lose him but not wanting to go.

qa.q: What did Ganga's teacher do that was right?
qa.a: The teacher listened calmly, told Ganga there was no blame on Ganga, called Ganga's mother at once, and reported the account to the cyber cell that afternoon.

qa.q: How might Ganga's mother have felt when the teacher called?
qa.a: Ganga's mother would likely feel frightened and protective, and relieved that Ganga told someone before meeting him.

grounding: A teen recalls an online friend slowly moving to private apps, photos and a meeting, and a teacher responding the same day.

passage:
Counsellor's note, Class 10, Wednesday.
Alka came in at lunch and asked about "a friend's problem". After a while she said it was hers. For two months she has chatted with "Dev", who says he is seventeen, from a gaming group. He moved their chat to a private app, asked about her home and school, then last week asked for a photo "just for me" and to meet at the mall on Saturday. She said she felt flattered at first and now feels stuck and sick, because she already sent a selfie in her uniform.
I told her clearly that none of this is her fault, and that coming to me was the right thing. She has not replied to him since.
Actions today: informed the safeguarding lead; called her mother, who came at 3 pm; with Alka's agreement we saved the chats, blocked and reported the account, and filed a complaint with the cyber-crime helpline. The Saturday meeting will not happen.
Nirmala

qa.q: Where did Dev ask to meet?
qa.a: At the mall on Saturday.

qa.q: How does Alka feel about the chats now?
qa.a: Alka felt flattered at first but now feels stuck and sick, worried about the selfie she already sent.

qa.q: What did Nirmala do after Alka spoke, and why does it matter?
qa.a: Nirmala told Alka she was not to blame, informed the safeguarding lead, called her mother, and saved, blocked and reported the account the same day, so the meeting will not happen.

qa.q: How might Alka's mother feel arriving at 3 pm?
qa.a: She would likely feel frightened and protective, but also relieved that Alka told someone and the Saturday meeting was stopped.

grounding: Shows a teen whose online contact moved to a private app and asked personal questions, a photo and a meeting, and a counsellor's same-day response that she is not to blame.
